# DropSpace v0.3.0-beta.31

<!-- update-summary: Keep lyric gaps stable, refine island placement and transitions, and expand the widget library and layout editor. -->

## Changes

- Keep matched lyrics visible through short gaps rather than reverting to the song title. Longer timestamped instrumental gaps show a subtle breathing indicator and return to the next lyric without collapsing the layout.
- Move the default island closer to the screen edge with an 8-DIP visual gap, and fit content to the monitor work area across DPI and aspect ratios.
- Use focus-independent Desktop Acrylic for the main window as well as the island, while retaining Windows accessibility and unsupported-material fallbacks.
- Add interruptible crossfades between island pages and per-layer translation/scale during expansion and collapse. Reduced motion removes spatial effects.
- Expand the widget catalog from 8 to 16: UTC clock, 25-minute focus timer, 5-minute countdown, system-disk free space, network-adapter status, calculator, pinned-items shortcut, and ISO week progress.
- Add layout landing previews, directional movement, explicit position/size application, a two-column widget catalog, and one-step undo.

- Redact credentials embedded in URL user-info from diagnostic logs.
- Correct word highlighting timestamps when enhanced LRC repeats a lyric line at multiple times.

## Compatibility and limits

Beta 30 is the immediate upgrade baseline. App identity, data directories and update channels remain unchanged; existing widget enum identifiers and saved layouts are preserved. New widgets are opt-in from the library.

Countdowns are session-only and do not send background completion notifications. Network status describes adapter connectivity, not a verified Internet connection. Windows may require opaque material for accessibility, disabled transparency or unsupported composition. Plain lyric files without line-end timing cannot identify every instrumental gap.

Windows build and installer validation are required for this release. Automated checks do not replace manual visual checks on physical mixed-DPI monitors or real music-player sessions.
